rationale: Unison Energy remains a qualifying active U.S. distributed-energy infrastructure platform. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III controls the business through Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III AIV U LP from the reported June 17, 2024 close. AIF/AIM Universal and Hunt are former owners. Unison's principal ESA model includes long-lived owned and operated microgrid assets, but the company also delivers customer-owned EPC, O&M and hybrid structures. Exact Tiger equity, rollover and current platform scale are disclosure gaps and must not be inferred.
recommendedChanges: Retain one Unison Energy canonical record and keep customer microgrids and project SPVs beneath it.
Record Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III as the active controlling owner through Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III AIV U LP from June 17, 2024, without claiming sole or 100% ownership.
Add American Infrastructure Funds/AIM Universal Holdings as a former controlling owner and Hunt Companies as a former minority owner, both ending at the reported Tiger close.
Qualify the operating model: Unison's primary ESA business finances, owns and operates long-term infrastructure, while it also offers customer-owned EPC, O&M and hybrid delivery.
Use the approximately 30 operating or signed-ESA projects and approximately 26 MW only as entry-date scale; current aggregate scale is not publicly disclosed.
Preserve the August 2026 Gaylord Pacific agreement as post-close evidence of active 20-year owned-EaaS development rather than an ownership transaction.
unresolvedQuestions: Tiger's exact equity percentage, governance rights and any founder or management rollover are not publicly disclosed.
Transaction value, primary-versus-secondary capital split and any legal effective date different from June 17, 2024 are not publicly disclosed.
Current owned megawatts, project count and the full project-SPV financing roster are not publicly disclosed.
